abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chitinase-3-like-protein 1 (CHI3L1), a low-abundance protein in normal tissues, is markedly upregulated in the pancreatic tumor microenvironment (TME), where it promotes fibrosis and immune evasion. Spatial transcriptomics revealed enrichment of CHI3L1 at tumor-stroma interfaces, suggesting that cell-cell interactions regulate CHI3L1 expression.
METHODS: We employed 2D and 3D multicellular culture models, incorporating pancreatic cancer cells, macrophages, and pancreatic stellate cells (PSCs), to recapitulate TME-mediated CHI3L1 induction. Mechanistic insights were gained through secretome profiling, chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), and methylation-specific PCR. The therapeutic potential of targeting identified axes was evaluated in an orthotopic pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) mouse model.
RESULTS: We identified CCL2, CXCL10, and SPARC as key secreted mediators during tumor-stroma crosstalk that cooperatively induced CHI3L1 expression in cancer cells via activation of NF-κB and STAT3. Specifically, inflammatory cytokines within the TME recruited macrophages to induce CCL2, which, in concert with PSCs, enhances CXCL10 and SPARC secretion. Mechanistically, NF-κB directly bound the CHI3L1 promoter, while STAT3 reduced DNA methyltransferase 1 levels, leading to promoter hypomethylation and epigenetic activation of CHI3L1. Clinically, high CHI3L1 expression correlated with the upregulated stromal CCL2, CXCL10, and SPARC levels, and the combined four-marker signature was an independent prognostic factor for both overall and disease-free survival in multivariable analysis. In vivo, blockade of the upstream stromal pathways (CCR2/CXCR3/TGFβR1) coupled with CHI3L1 neutralization reduced tumor growth and remodeled the immunosuppressive microenvironment in immunocompetent PDAC models.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings uncover a cooperative multicellular signaling network that orchestrates CHI3L1 expression in cancer via transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming. Disrupting these upstream stromal pathways concurrently with CHI3L1 neutralization was associated with reduced T-cell exhaustion, offering a promising combinatorial approach for PDAC immunotherapy.
key_points_ko: CCL2, CXCL10, SPARC는 NF-κB와 STAT3 경로를 활성화하여 암세포에서 CHI3L1 발현을 협력적으로 유도합니다.
높은 CHI3L1 발현은 다변량 분석에서 전체 생존기간과 무병 생존기간 모두에 대한 독립적인 예후 인자였습니다.
동물 모델에서 상위 기질 경로 차단과 CHI3L1 중화를 병행했을 때 종양 성장이 감소하고 면역억제성 미세환경이 재조절되었습니다.
summary_ko: 본 연구는 췌장암(pancreatic cancer) 미세환경에서 CHI3L1 단백질의 발현을 유도하는 세포 간 신호 전달 네트워크를 조사했습니다. 2차원 및 3차원 세포 배양 모델과 쥐 모델을 활용하여, 종양과 기질 세포 간의 상호작용이 NF-κB와 STAT3를 통해 CHI3L1 발현을 높이는 과정을 분석했습니다. 연구 결과, 상위 기질 경로를 차단하고 CHI3L1을 중화하면 종양 성장이 줄어들고 면역억제성 미세환경이 개선되었습니다. 임상적으로 높은 CHI3L1 발현은 전체 생존기간 및 무병 생존기간과 연관된 독립적 예후 인자임을 확인했습니다.
title: Stromal CCL2/CXCL10/SPARC axes drive pro-tumor CHI3L1 expression for microenvironmental modulation in pancreatic cancer progression and therapeutic innovation
title_ko: 기질(stroma)의 CCL2/CXCL10/SPARC 축이 췌장암 진행 및 치료 혁신을 위한 미세환경 조절에서 종양 촉진성 CHI3L1 발현을 유도합니다
